cancel().notice: executor (BI) or any party may cancel a pending atom (task #3 correction, lead decision 5b / backend spec F5: BI is the settlement agent and must be able to clean up a stuck trade, not just the trade's own parties). `nonReentrant` added for defense-in-depth consistency with execute()/simulate() (delta-audit lead, 2026-10-05) -- not exploitable today (execute() flips status before its external calls; simulate() unconditionally reverts, unwinding any nested call into this function), but cancel() was the one Pending-gated mutator relying on those OTHER functions' internal ordering instead of guarding itself. Task #8: status flips to Cancelled unconditionally (recorded regardless of how many legs actually had anything to release), THEN each leg in `_cancelOperations` is attempted, isolated (one leg's revert/failure never blocks another's, and never blocks the status change itself, which already happened).

execute().notice: Only `executor` (BI) may execute -- unchanged from task #2. Preserves upstream's atomicity: status flips to Executed before any external call, so a reentrant call back into execute() would already see status != Pending even without `nonReentrant`.

retryRelease(uint256).notice: Audit fix: cancel()'s per-leg release was one-shot -- a leg whose release call legitimately failed (as opposed to being skipped as not-delegated/inactive) had no recourse, since `status` is terminal once Cancelled and no other function could ever call Noto for that lock again. Callable by executor or any party, same gate as cancel(), only while `status == Cancelled` (retrying before a cancel makes no sense, and retrying after Executed is impossible by construction).

simulate().notice: Simulates every operation without committing state, same shape as upstream. Task #3 correction (lead): the task-#2 party/executor gate on this function does NOT protect confidentiality and that claim is withdrawn. `eth_call`'s `from` field is unauthenticated -- any caller can set it to any address, including a party's or the executor's, and bypass the check trivially. More fundamentally, `getOperations()` already exposes every operation's target+callData with no gate at all, so a caller can reconstruct everything this function would reveal with its own, entirely separate `eth_call` (`{from: <this atom's address>, to: op.contractAddress, data: op.callData}`) straight at the target, which never touches this contract or its gate (confirmed by audit delta pass 2026-10-05). The gate below is kept as a UX guard only -- it stops an honest caller's own tooling from invoking the wrong atom by mistake, or from getting a confusing error on a trade it was never party to -- not as an access-control or confidentiality boundary; none exists for this function, by design.
